title: The warship that sank in 1,300 metres
caption:
Sweden's mightiest warship failed its stability test, so they sailed it anyway. It made it 1,300 metres. ⚓
Too many cannons high up and too little ballast low down put the centre of gravity too high: one gust and the open gunports took on water.
Would you have stopped the launch, or kept your head down and kept your job?
first_comment: The king wanted more guns. The ocean wanted the ship. Ocean won 1-0 🌊 Who's really to blame: the king or the shipbuilders?
sources: Vasa Museum (Vasamuseet), 'The ship' and 'Why did Vasa sink?': sank on her maiden voyage on 10 August 1628 after about 1,300 m; 64 guns on two gun decks; too little ballast and a high centre of gravity; water entered the open lower gunports; about 30 people died
Vasa Museum / Military History Matters, 'Back to the drawing board: Vasa': the pre-sailing stability test in which 30 men ran across the deck was stopped after three runs because she heeled so much
